questions.q_en: Which of the following is a fundamental unit?
questions.solution_en:
• Metre is a fundamental unit for length in the SI system.

• Newton is a derived unit of force.

• Joule is a derived unit of energy.

• Pascal is a derived unit of pressure.

Further Insight:

• Units

• A unit is a fixed standard quantity used to measure other quantities of the same kind.

• Types of Units:

○ Fundamental Units: Cannot be expressed in terms of other physical quantities. Examples: Length (meter), Mass (kilogram), Time (second), etc.

○ Derived Units: Derived from fundamental units. Examples: Area (square meter), Volume (cubic meter), Force (newton).

questions.q_en: In which of the following systems is the unit of mass measured in grams?
questions.solution_en:
• In the CGS system, mass is measured in grams.

• In the MKS system and SI system, mass is measured in kilograms.

• In the FPS system, mass is measured in pounds.

Further Insight:

• Earlier systems of Measurement included:

○ CGS System: Length in centimeters, mass in grams, time in seconds.

○ MKS System: Length in meters, mass in kilograms, time in seconds.

○ FPS System: Length in feet, mass in pounds, time in seconds.

• SI Units: The most widely used system today, providing consistency across scientific disciplines.

questions.q_en: How many meters is 1 light year approximately equal to?
questions.solution_en:
• 1 light year is approximately 9.46 X 10¹⁵ meters.

• 3.26 X 10¹⁶ meters refers to parsec.

• 1.496 X 10¹¹ meters refers to an astronomical unit.

• 3.00 X 10⁸ m/s is the speed of light in m/s.

Further Insight:

• Astronomical Unit (AU): Mean distance between Earth and Sun.

○ 1 AU = 1.496 X 10¹¹ m.

• Light Year: Distance light travels in one year.

○ 1 Light Year = 9.46 X 10¹⁵ m.

• Parsec: Used for measuring distances outside the solar system.

○ 1 Parsec = 3.26 light years = 3.08 X 10¹⁶ m.
